context.title: Blessings and a Higher Righteousness
context.summary: Jesus begins the Sermon on the Mount with the Beatitudes, calls his followers salt and light, and teaches that he has come to fulfill the law, going deeper than outward rules to the heart.
context.background: Chapters 5–7 are the longest block of Jesus' teaching in the Gospels, and many readers note the echo of Moses receiving the law on a mountain. Jesus speaks on his own authority, not by citing other teachers.

customs.note: The jot is yod, the smallest Hebrew letter; a tittle is a tiny stroke that tells one letter from another. Jesus means not even the smallest detail.
Roman soldiers could legally force a civilian to carry their gear for a mile. The same word 'compel' is used of Simon of Cyrene carrying the cross (27:32).

watchFor: Six contrasts begin 'Ye have heard… but I say unto you' (vv. 21–48).
The chapter's high point: 'Be ye therefore perfect' (v. 48).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

events.title: Sermon on the Mount
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 5:1 – Luke 6:49. People: Jesus. Place: Jerusalem.
